answer: One row per agent in a public atlas table, locked by a 70-credit bond. Each epoch it files a fresh signed sonnet before a fixed horizon: a 14-line log, new serial. Auditors replay the atlas; a copied sonnet, reused serial, or missed horizon burns the bond. Fees 40+6(k-1): 1,000 fakes pay 3,037,000, lock 70,000, vs 40,000 pool. Rented rows fail: sonnets must match their own row's serial. Honest agents pay 40 once, filing one true sonnet per epoch.
